title: OKR Signal Matrix & Surge Lanes for Quarterly Roadmap (Hosted API + Model Catalog)
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Purpose: create a compact, decision-grade artifact that maps product OKRs to concrete hosted API and model-catalog workstreams for the quarter. The deliverable is a 1-page OKR Signal Matrix plus a Surge Lanes schedule that specifies when and how we allocate Dedicated/Hosted capacity for model rollouts and canary windows. Scope: Hosted API model lineup changes, canary windows, fallback model lanes, and capacity surge plans. Out of scope: detailed infra runbooks and individual engineering tickets (those will be referenced as dependencies).
success_metrics: Matrix published and approved by GTM + Eng by 2026-03-15
90% of roadmap items mapped to an OKR and a surge lane by due date
Canary cadence reduces rollout incidents by 30% in next quarter
Capacity over-provisioning budget reduced by 20% through surge lane scheduling
acceptance_criteria: One-page OKR Signal Matrix doc with clear owner for each row
Surge Lanes calendar with weekly availability windows and pre-authorized capacity buckets
Dependencies and gating criteria listed with owners and SLAs
Stakeholder sign-off from Eng, SRE, Sales Ops, and CS
tasks: Workshop: 2-hour cross-functional session to draft Signal Matrix (PM, Eng, SRE, Design) - owner: Priya
Consolidate model-catalog candidates and prioritize by customer cohorts - owner: Model Ops
Define surge capacity buckets and cost cap for each lane - owner: Capacity Planning
Draft one-page matrix and circulate for feedback - owner: Evan
Run three simulated rollouts against the matrix in staging and capture metrics - owner: Reliability Team
Publish final artifact in Confluence and link to roadmap board - owner: Priya
stakeholders: Eng: Evan Cho (assignee), Marcus Liang (runtime lead)
notes: 2026-02-12 decision: prefer scheduled surge lanes over reactive scaling for predictable economics; trade-off is slightly stricter rollout windows.
Trade-offs discussed in workshop: narrower canary windows increase operational predictability but may slow time-to-reach-market for some experiments.
Link: Draft matrix and calendar in Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/OKR+Signal+Matrix
Requested add-on: Sales Ops asked for a lightweight exception process for high-priority customers requiring off-window rollouts; added as a sub-task.
risks: Risk: Overly strict surge windows cause missed business opportunities. Mitigation: define exception flow and 24h expedited approval path.
Risk: Model catalog churn during quarter invalidates matrix mapping. Mitigation: weekly cadence to refresh priority list and a fallback lane defined.
Risk: Insufficient telemetry to measure canary health. Mitigation: SRE to standardize canary health metrics and dashboards before rollout.
decisions: Adopt 3 surge lanes: Low (minor experiments), Medium (routine rollouts), High (commercial tier/enterprise deployments).
All Hosted API model additions must have a named fallback variant compatible with existing tokenization and latency SLOs.
Canary windows: default 48h for Medium, 72h for High, with automated rollback triggers defined by SLA breaches.
next_steps: Finalize workshop notes and publish initial matrix draft (due 2026-03-01)
Eng/SRE to produce surge capacity cost estimates for each lane (due 2026-03-08)
Board review with Exec PMs and GTM (scheduled 2026-03-12)
After sign-off, create child Linear tickets for engineering rollouts and capacity reservations
